      Build  ·  Headphones recommended  ·  Procedurally generated audio & visuals
      Night shift · Site Kestrel, Sublevel 6 · 02:00 AM
      Survive until 6:00 AM

      You are the night guard, buried under the mountain. Something tall and pale has broken out of its cell, the facility is in lockdown, and the surface lift stays sealed until the day shift arrives at 6:00 AM.

      Your mission: stay alive until dawn — then make it onto the lift. Every hour it gets worse. It crawls. It hears everything. At 4:00 the power goes, and in the last hour it can follow you into the vents. Lockers only buy you time.

      It is not alone. A little after 2:30 something else gets up out of the Morgue — slow, humming a lullaby. It never chases you, but stay away from it: near it you start to hallucinate, and you can't trust anything you see or hear.

      Want out sooner? Find the three keycards, restore main power and upload the breach report, and you can open the lift yourself.

      You're not the only one left. Three of the voices on the tapes are still alive down here, hiding where their tapes say they were. Find them, talk to them — each can help you — and bring them to the lift.

      Someone has been taking pictures down here. Eight Polaroids are pinned to walls around Sublevel 6 — somewhere different every time you play. You start with a flashlight, and the Warden is already awake.

      Find all eight, then get to the surface lift. Every photo you take makes it worse: faster, sharper-eared, and at four the power fails. The Sleepwalker comes out after the second. The clock is running — beat your best time.

      The service lift was meant to take you up. It went down — and a cable snapped. You are on Sublevel 7, the Mimicry wing: a museum nobody visits, full of mannequins, dolls and plaster casts of faces.

      Subject M looks like all the others. It only moves when nobody is looking at it — keep it on your screen, in the light, and it can't take a step. Look away, let your torch flicker, or let the lights brown out, and it's on you. Two of you watching it is safer than one.

      Your mission: find three fuses hidden somewhere new every run, restore the power in Gallery Control, call the freight lift — then hold out until it comes. It is plastic: it comes apart under a crowbar, and it hates fire.

      The lift didn't stop at the Gallery. It dropped all the way to Sublevel 8 — the deep power station that keeps all of Site Kestrel alive — and the cable snapped. The turbines have stopped. Only the red emergency lamps are left, and they are going out one at a time.

      Subject S lives in the dark between them. It cannot go where the light is: lamps, flares, fire and your torch beam are walls to it. Hold your torch on it and it screams and pulls back — do it enough and it scatters. But it waits where the light ends, it puts the lamps out, and your torch dims when it's close. Steel goes straight through it.

      Your mission: restart the three turbines (stay at each console until it spins up — it's loud), throw the main breaker in Station Control, and call the Surface Express. When you do, every light in the station dies at once. Light a flare. Survive until it comes.

      The lift kept falling. Sublevel 9 — Lantern Bio-Containment, where they grew something in tanks. It grew back, and it has been breeding. This floor is not one monster. It is a nest.

      Crawlers hunt in packs and come at you from different sides — they hate fire. Screamer pods on the walls watch the corridors: if one sees you it screams, and everything on the floor comes. Some of the supply crates are mimics. Spitters lob acid from across the room. And something huge is kept in the Holding Pens.

      Your mission: find three Lantern cultures (somewhere new every run), run them through the sequencer and hold the lab while it works, then burn the three brood nests — at their purge valves, or with your own fire. Burning the last one lets the Butcher out. Reroute power at two junctions, call the Quarantine Lift, and hold out until it comes.

      Below the Hive there is no facility — only the old Kestrel mine, and what the brood grew from. Sublevel 10, the Root: caves, a flooded lake, a chasm with one bridge, and in the middle of it all a chamber with a heartbeat.

      The Visitor lives down here too. Something very tall and white that came in through a hole in the roof. It is slow and almost silent — listen for the claw it drags. It ducks to get through the corridors and cannot fit in a vent, but it can skewer you through a locker door: hide in the vents, not the lockers. Two hard hits stun it for five seconds.

      Your mission: charge the three survey pylons (stay with each one — it's loud) to break the seals on the Heart, then kill the Mother: her arms come down where the red rings are — get out of them — and her three glowing sacs are the only thing that hurts her. Then the caves come down. Run for the old mine elevator before the collapse buries you.

      Tonight you don't leave the security office. From midnight to 6:00 AM you keep watch from Desk B: ten cameras (, then 1–0 or the map to switch), one door (the red switch on the desk, or at the door) and one vent in the north wall.

      The Warden walks room to room toward your door — you'll see it pass the West Hall or the South Hall. Shut the door before it gets there and it slams it and leaves; leave it open and it comes in. Later (2 AM on Normal) the Mannequin sets off from Medical: it only moves when nobody is watching it — on a camera, or through the open doorway with your own eyes. After that (3 AM on Normal) the brood crawls down the vent: hold your flashlight () on the grate until it backs off.

      Every camera you watch and every second the door is shut drains the power. At 0% the lights die, the cameras go dark, the door slides open and won't close — and something starts to hum outside it. Make the power last until six. Online, the power and the door are shared: split the jobs.

      Tonight you are the Warden. You start in Containment; the night shift is out on its rounds (one of them always at Desk B). Four guards on Normal (three on Easy, five on Nightmare) are pulling fuses out of the rooms — the glowing boxes — and when they have enough, the blast door opens and they run for the surface lift through the Lift Lobby.

      Click to swipe: a guard in reach is caught. SCREECH: you hear every one of them for 6 seconds, through the walls, and the ones close to you freeze. POUNCE: a long leap. The guards hide in lockers — a heartbeat means one is close; tears the door open. They run when they see you, and their flashlights blind you if you come at them from the front.

      If half of them get out, the hunt is lost. Catch them all — or keep them inside until 6:00 AM. Online, everyone is a Warden and you hunt together: there are more guards for more of you, and the host decides every catch.

      One expedition, five floors, in order: Sublevel 6 (the Night Shift), 7 (the Gallery), 8 (the Blackout), 9 (the Hive) and 10 (the Root). Each floor is the real one — clear it the way you would on its own.

      Between floors you ride the lift: see how the team is, use the shared med kits and battery packs, read what you found — then EXTRACT (bank everything, the expedition ends) or vote to CONTINUE (deeper floors pay more, nothing is banked yet). Online, going deeper needs more than half the team; a tie or the clock running out means extract.

      Your health, battery, spares and weapons come down with you. [J] uses a med kit on a floor. Lost on a floor: one retry from the last lift (it costs 20% of the unbanked bounty) — or the expedition ends and you keep 25%. Leaving in the middle of a floor counts as a failed attempt. A dossier page is hidden on every floor.

      Modifiers · harder, and they pay more

      You sit at Desk B with the camera network of Sublevel 6. Learn what every room looks like — where each thing stands, which lamps are lit, what its clock says, what it sounds like. When something in a room changes, report it: which room, and what changed.

      A right report keeps the system running; a wrong one, or one you miss, costs INTEGRITY. At 0% the shift is lost. Cameras break down too: a FAULT drops a camera's signal bars, and a RESET fixes it — an anomaly never touches the signal. COMPARE shows a room as it was at the start of the shift. Both cost power.

      Seven shifts, each with more cameras, more kinds of change, and THE INTRUSION. Online, the team watches together: a report waits a few seconds for a teammate to confirm or veto it, and the host decides.

      RUN

      MAP

      Sublevel 6 is half-way through a renovation: the lights are on and there's paint everywhere — murals, tarps, panels, rugs, a colour to every room. You are a thick little stickman, factory orange. You have 25 seconds (Normal) before the Warden wakes up in Containment.

      Press [L] to lock yourself in place: your mouse is free, the camera turns round you from any angle (drag the view, scroll to zoom) and you drag on yourself to paint — down to a FINE brush a centimetre wide, on any part of you ([ and ] change the size); click a wall to pick up its colour. [L] again and you can move. [Esc] (or [B]) opens the whole paint shop: fill a piece, patterns, mixing. picks up the colour of whatever you face. is the CHAMELEON SPRAY: back against a wall, crouch, and every part of you turns the colour (and the pattern) that's behind it. [Shift] swaps to an over-the-shoulder camera (run with Space in this mode); pauses.

      The Warden doesn't see you — it sees what doesn't match what's behind you, from where it stands: colour, light, open space, which side of you it's looking at, and above all movement. Crouch, freeze against a wall your colour and it can walk right past you — a couple of metres away — and when it does you get a CLOSE CALL (and coins). Your CAMO meter says how well you blend in from where it could be standing. But it hears you, it smells anyone who stays in one place too long, a near-miss colour shows up close, and nothing survives it walking straight into you. Lose it, and it only knows where it last saw you: break its line of sight, move, freeze. Throw the breakers (hold — loud), then get to the Surface Lift. Online, a caught player is caged in Containment until a teammate frees them; the team wins if half of you get out.

      No two rounds are the same. The Warden wakes up as one of three: THE STALKER (slow, careful, a sharp eye), THE PROWLER (fast rounds, never looks for long) or THE LISTENER (half-blind, but every sound brings it running). It remembers where it glimpsed something odd, and comes back to look. A minute or so in, something happens — named and timed at the top of the screen: a BLACKOUT (it sees less, hears more), a SEARCHLIGHT DRONE (stay out of its light), THE SLEEPWALKER (never let it touch you: it screams) or a FRESH COAT (a room is repainted: re-spray). Three gold paint tins are hidden against the walls — collect them over your rounds for new paints — and every round has a bonus job. Online, from a cage: calls for help (it hears that too) and watches a teammate; the free see FREE <NAME> over the cage.

      Two maps. SUBLEVEL 6 is the facility, mid-renovation. THE COLOUR WORKS (Sublevel 5) is the paint factory upstairs: every room its own colours — earth pigments, the primaries of the Mixing Hall's vats, the Tint Lab's pastels, the Showroom's swatch walls. Hide behind the Drying Room's hanging sheets (they hide you; they don't stop anyone walking through), and step into a SPRAY BOOTH: and you're coated head to toe in its colours — it hisses, and the Warden knows what booths are for. Caught, you go to the Wash Bay; the way out is the Goods Lift. Online, the host picks the map.

      The lift takes you down to the lobby of THE HOLLOWAY, an old hotel three floors deep, and won't take you back up. One room after the next, every door numbered — 0001 to 0100. The last one is the way out. The rooms are furnished differently every run.

      Walk into a door and it opens. Some are locked: the key is somewhere in the room you're in — on a dresser, on a table, in a drawer. Open drawers for gold, batteries (your light runs down), bandages ([1]) and vitamins ([2]); a lockpick opens any locked door; a crucifix holds off whatever would have killed you, once.

      When the lights flicker and you hear something far back: HIDE in a wardrobe and stay there until it has gone past (and sometimes it comes back). In the dark, if something whispers "psst", turn round and look at it. Never look at the eyes. When eyes open on the walls — get ready to run. In the library at 50 something blind listens for you: walk softly, find the books and the librarian's note, open the padlock. Room 100: put the power back on, then run. Online, up to four of you, together; you're all the Night Guard.

      DAYS
      RUN

      You're lost in the Hollow Creek woods with a dying fire. Last 99 nights. By day the thing in the woods sleeps: go out and gather — wood off the dead trees and fallen logs, scrap from the junk piles and the wrecks, berries, whatever's left in the crates at the ranger's cabin, the old lodge, the hunter's shack, the trailer and the sawmill. Bring it back to the bench at camp and put it on the pile.

      Feed the fire (wood or fuel, at the fire pit): it won't walk into its light, and the more you feed it the bigger it grows — five levels, each pushing the fog back further. At the bench, make things: bear traps ([1]) that hold it where it stands, noise lures ([2]) that send it after a rattle, flares ([3]) and lantern posts ([5]) it won't come near, batteries, a bigger pack, steel traps; build the bench up for more. Eat ([4]) or you'll starve — cook three berries into a hot meal at the fire.

      At night it comes looking. It hears everything you do and sees your torch from far off — but hold your beam on its face and it can't stand it. Every night it gets faster, sharper, bolder. Four people are lost in these woods: find them and walk them home to the fire. Dozens of goals ([J]) pay coins and stay done. Your run is saved at every dawn. No weapons — none to find, none to bring. Online, up to four of you.

      The day shift is never coming. There is no lift, no keycard, no way out — only the night, and how long you can last in it.

      Every hour (about a minute and a half) you get a spare battery — and you must choose one of two curses. They stack: a faster Warden, sharper ears, brownouts, open vents, phantoms everywhere… Every run is different. Beat your longest night.

      Field manual
      How to Play

      Controls

      W A S DMove (arrow keys also work) MouseLook — click START to capture the mouse ShiftSprint — fast, drains stamina, very loud Ctrl / CCrouch — hold Ctrl or toggle with C. Quiet, needed for vents. (Careful with Ctrl: Ctrl+W closes a browser tab) TFlashlight — limited battery FYour character's ability (see Characters). Each has a cooldown, shown bottom-left RSwap in a spare battery; with no spares, hold to crank (noisy) EInteract: doors, items, notes, switches, lockers MToggle minimap (shows explored areas) HHint — highlights the next thing you need in yellow (it also happens on its own when you're stuck; turn it off in Settings) ClickAttack with the weapon in your hand (no weapon: punch) V / Right clickPunch. It barely hurts the Warden, but a few hits — or one as it lunges — stun it for a few seconds. 1–7 / QSwitch weapons (or the mouse wheel): 1 crowbar · 2 axe · 3 shotgun · 4 flare gun · 5 molotovs · 6 flintlock · 7 smoke grenades. Press a weapon's number again to put it away. At the Business Man's table, 1–5 pick a trade SpaceIn a locker: hold the door shut when it pulls on it — press on every pull, on the beat GCo-op: mark a spot for your team Hold SpaceSkip a camera cutscene P / EscPause and release the mouse SettingsEvery key above can be changed: Settings → Controls

      Surviving the Warden

      • Daily Contracts. Three jobs a day (title screen → Daily Contracts) from all over the game — survive the Night Shift, reach door 30, win a round of MECHA CAMO… Each pays coins at the end of the run that does it; all three in a day pays a bonus that grows with your streak. One free swap a day for a job you don't fancy.
      • Survivors (Night Shift). Three of the people on the voice logs are still alive, hiding where their tapes say: Rosa Ortiz in the vent behind Storage, Pete Doyle in the Generator Hall, Dr. Adebayo in a morgue drawer (listen for the knocking). Found a tape? H points to its owner. E on one to talk; E again: "follow me" or "wait here". Rosa's radio warns you when it's coming your way; ask Doyle in the Generator Hall and he gets the power on (after 4:00, the emergency lights); Dr. Adebayo stitches you up (every 60 s) and gets a downed teammate back up. They freeze when it's near — but it hears them walk, and if it walks into one of them, they're gone. Whoever is with you when the lift leaves gets out: coins, rank points and three achievements.
      • Characters. Everyone starts as the Night Guard. Character Roll (title screen) spins for one of 36 characters in seven rarities — Common 39.99%, Rare 27%, Epic 16%, Legendary 10%, Mythic 5%, Special 2% and ULTIMATE 0.01% (the odds are on the roll screen). Three of the Specials change what you carry: the Tarnished starts with a sword (three clean cuts stun it) and a shield that blocks standing still and charges on the run; Glitch fights with a glitching fist that leaves the monster weaker to every blow, can't hold any weapon but the shotgun, and skips 8 m untouchable; the Demolitionist carries frag and stun grenades in slots 1 and 2, turns a shotgun into a grenade launcher, has no melee at all — and his breach charge throws anything away from him, at the cost of 30 health. Your first spin is free; after that each costs 100 coins, earned only by playing: escaping, staying alive, completing objectives, reviving and healing teammates, achievements. Harder difficulties pay more. Rarity is how rare a character is — not how strong: each has a real strength, a real weakness and one ability on F.
      • The new hires. The Sportsman (150 stamina) spikes a volleyball that knocks a monster back and staggers it. The Hybrid is always the monsters' last choice, and sensors and traps never notice them. The Scientist turns a smoke grenade into a gas bomb (a green cloud that eats at whatever is in it) or a molotov into napalm (a bigger fire: a monster in it is slowed, and hits half as hard for a while after). The Robot carries only a crowbar and smoke, heals twice as fast, gets a downed teammate up at once — but can't be revived itself — and its SERVO LOCK holds a monster still for 4.5 s while everyone runs. The Builder can't swing a crowbar or axe or fire a shotgun, but raises a barricade (100 HP, two at a time) in 3 s: your team climbs through, the monsters have to smash it, and nothing hits you through it. The Hacker (Special) sees three tasks at once, works 1.5× faster, and can lock down the room they're in for 10 s — nothing gets in.
      • ULTIMATE (one spin in ten thousand). An Ultimate has a second power on X. AETHER, THE STARBORN: NOVA (25 stamina) blasts back everything within 9 m and shields everyone near him (half damage for 6 s); SUPERNOVA — he rises, untouchable, everything within 22 m frozen, then detonates: 120 damage and a 4 s stun to every monster in reach, downed teammates back on their feet, everyone else healed. After it he's burned out for 10 s (no stamina, slow, no sprint) and it takes 150 s to charge again — and he glows: monsters see and hear him from much further away. NYX, THE ECLIPSE: UMBRA VEIL hides her and anyone near from the monsters; TOTAL ECLIPSE blinds every monster on the floor for 8 s while the team sees them through walls — but her own light dies for 10 s after.
      • Reading an attack. Every monster telegraphs its blows: the Warden raises its claws (or coils to leap, or draws its arm back to throw), the Mannequin's joints creak as its arms come up, the Shade's arms reach out of the smoke. When one is coming at you, a red edge on your screen shows which side and a warning sound plays. Step out of reach, break its line, put your light on the Shade, or turn and look at the Mannequin — a blow only lands if it actually connects. Then it needs a moment to recover.
      • Damage and difficulty. A standard hit does 20 on Easy, 35 on Normal, 50 on Hard and 65 on Nightmare (against 100 HP; your character's health and defences change that). Your HP, every hit you take and the difficulty are on the HUD. Harder difficulties see further, hear more, chase faster, search longer, telegraph less, heal you slower — and on Hard and Nightmare the monsters work together.
      • Down, not out (co-op). Online, running out of health puts you DOWN: you can crawl, and you bleed out unless a teammate holds E beside you (a Medic, Phoenix or an Engineer in Overdrive does it faster — or from further away). Bled out, you're caught.
      • The facility bites back. Red circles on corridor floors are ceiling motion sensors: walk or run through one and it shrieks for everything on the floor to hear — crouch through, go round, or hold E under it to pull its wires. Sparking wall panels arc every few seconds: keep clear. Volt's EMP kills every hazard around him.
      • The Business Man. Every time the night gets worse — a new hour, a floor's next step — a tall man in a good suit, with no face you can make out, is suddenly open for business in one of the rooms (a gold $ on your map). While he is there nothing big comes into his room. He trades the coins you roll characters with — and the weapons you carry — for better ones: the Flintlock (twelve shots that will never be replenished, every one stuns), sharpened weapons (+30%), smoke, ammunition, a field dressing. Then he's gone.
      • Smoke grenades lie around every floor, somewhere new every run (7). Throw one: anything that walks into the cloud is lost for ten seconds — it can't find anyone, and it can't hurt anyone.
      • Fighting it. Face the Warden armed and you can choose to FIGHT: a crowbar fight is Fight for your life, an axe fight Fight to kill. With nobody on their feet within 50 m — and always when you play alone — it is THE LAST DANCE, and you get the health for it: +100% on Easy, +200% on Normal, +400% on Hard and Nightmare, until it goes down. Kill the floor's monster for good (the Warden, the Mannequin, the Shade — burn it away three times — the Butcher, the Visitor) and every coin of the run is worth ×5.
      • The Visitor (Sublevels 9 and 10). Something very tall and white that is not from here: it came in through a hole it punched in the roof and went down to where it's darkest. It is slower than the Warden and almost silent — listen for the claw it drags. It stoops to get through corridors, can't fit in a vent, and puts its claw straight through a locker door: hide in the vents, never the lockers. Two hard hits stun it for five seconds.
      • Pity. Bad luck runs out: the Character Roll counts your spins since you last got each rarity (it's on the roll screen). Ten spins without a Legendary or better, and the next one is a Legendary or better; 40 for a Mythic, 90 for a Special — and 500 for an ULTIMATE, which gets more likely with every spin after 400. Your counts are kept in your save.
      • Codes. Got a code? Title screen → Codes (or the Codes button on the Character Roll): type it in for coins or free spins. Each code works once on your save.
      • THE INFESTANT (online co-op only). Play with friends and, after a while, something else comes in with you: it wears one of your team — their face, their kit, their name over its head, a light in its hand — and it goes for whoever is alone. Up close it comes apart and strikes, then runs, and comes back later as someone else. Tells: its light lights nothing, its feet make no sound, and when it thinks nobody is watching its head goes over too far. Hold your flashlight on it and it burns, shrieks and flees; hit it and it flees; burn it enough and it's gone for the floor. Stay together and it only watches.
      • Build 18's new hires. KAIROS, THE LAST SECOND (ULTIMATE): REWIND takes him back to where he stood four seconds ago, with any health he lost since (it never takes health away); CHRONO HALT on X stops every monster on the floor for 6 s — then TIME DEBT, 8 s of taking 50% more damage. PYRO (Special): INFERNO, a 7.5 m jet of fire that burns, drives back and leaves the floor alight; fireproof — no fire, molotov or napalm hurts him — but his tanks make him slower and louder. TRAPPER (Special): BEAR TRAP, up to three on the floor; the first monster to step in one is clamped for 3.5 s and hurt, the team hears it, and he sees every monster through the walls for 4 s.
      • The deeper floors (New Game → Deeper): Sublevel 7, the Gallery — a museum of mannequins where one of them only moves while nobody looks at it: keep it in your light, find three fuses, power the freight lift. Sublevel 8, the Blackout — a power station gone dark, where the Shade lives between the lights: torch beams, flares and fire burn it, lamps keep it out, and it puts the lamps out to reach you. Restart three turbines, throw the main breaker, call the Surface Express — and survive the dark until it comes. Sublevel 9, the Hive — a bio-lab that grew a brood: crawler packs that flank you, screamer pods that call the rest, mimics among the supplies, spitters, and the Butcher (knock it down and keep hitting it while it's down: it gets up weaker, and the third time it stays down). Find three cultures, run the sequencer, burn three nests, reroute the power and hold the Lobby until the Quarantine Lift comes. Sublevel 10, the Root — the mine under everything: charge three pylons (one is missing its power cell), kill the Mother by bursting her three sacs while her arms come down in the red rings, then outrun the collapse to the old mine elevator — a different way out is buried every time.
      • THE ANOMALY (New Game → The Anomaly, solo or online): Desk B and the camera network of Sublevel 6. opens the cameras: 1–0 or ← → to switch, the mouse wheel to zoom. Learn each room — its objects, lamps, doors, clock and sound. When something changes, [R] REPORT it: the room, then what changed (1–0), Enter to file; [N] ALL CLEAR answers an AUDIT. Right keeps the system up; wrong or missed costs INTEGRITY — 0% ends the shift. A FAULT drops a camera's signal bars: [T] RESET it. [C] COMPARE shows the room at the start of the shift. When two cameras disagree (a SIGNAL CONFLICT), the one whose time stamp has stopped is a recording. If something reaches CAM 12, shut your door ([G]). Online, a report waits a few seconds for a teammate to confirm (Y) or veto (X). Seven shifts make a week; ENDLESS keeps going. Settings has the feed effects, captions for the microphones, and their volume.
      • THE DESCENT (New Game → The Descent, solo or online): one expedition down through all five floors — the Night Shift, the Gallery, the Blackout, the Hive and the Root, each exactly as you know it. Between floors the lift stops: see the team's condition, use a med kit or a battery from the shared supplies (one requisition per lift buys a med kit from your own bounty), read the evidence you found, and vote: EXTRACT (take the bounty home) or CONTINUE (deeper floors pay more). CONTINUE needs more than half the team; a tie, silence or the countdown running out means EXTRACT. What you carry goes down with you — health, batteries, weapons, ammo. Nothing is paid until you get out: the coins from each floor are your unsecured bounty, and a wipe keeps only 25% of it — unless you spend your one retry (from the last lift, for 20% of the bounty). Each floor hides one evidence page (a grey folder). Clear the Root to finish the expedition. uses a med kit on a floor. Modifiers on the briefing (Iron, Lean, Dark) make it harder and pay more. Alone, the expedition is saved at every lift and can be resumed from the title; leaving mid-floor counts as a failed attempt.
      • Five modes on Sublevel 6 (pick one when you press New Game): The Night Shift — survive until 6:00 AM; The Polaroids — find 8 photos hidden somewhere new every run, each one making it worse, then race to the lift (there is a Daily layout to compete on); Endless Night — no dawn, a new curse every hour (press 1 or 2 to choose), survive as long as you can; The Watch (Build 19) — midnight to 6 AM without leaving Desk B; The Hunt (Build 20, solo or online) — you are the Warden.
      • The Hunt: you play the monster. Click to swipe (a guard in reach is caught), SCREECH (you hear every guard for 6 s, through the walls; the ones close by freeze), POUNCE (a long leap that ends in a swipe), on a locker tears it open. Red marks show the guards you hear. The guards pull fuses; enough of them and the blast door opens and they run for the surface lift. Their flashlights blind you if they see you coming. If half of them get out, the hunt is lost; if they're still inside at 6 AM, you win.
      • 100 Doors: walk into a door to open it; locked ones need the key from the room you're in (or a lockpick). Drawers hold gold, batteries, bandages ([1]), vitamins ([2]), lockpicks and, rarely, a crucifix. Flickering lights = SURGE (or REBOUND, which comes back): get in a wardrobe until it's past — but not for too long. In a dark room, "psst" = HISS behind you: look at it. Purple light = THE EYES: look away. Eyes on the walls = THE SEEKER is near: when it climbs out, run through the doors and around the black pools. The library (50): find five books and the note on the desk; the note gives the order, the books the numbers — type them into the padlock. THE BLIND ONE hears footsteps (crouch near it); if it opens your wardrobe, press A/D as each heartbeat reaches the line. Room 100: the breaker key is on a crate; set every switch to its lamp (a wrong switch is loud), then run for the way out. points to the next door, key or book. No map.
      • The Hollow Woods (New Game → The Hollow Woods, solo or online): survive 99 nights. By day, gather ( on dead trees, fallen logs, junk piles, wrecks, berry bushes and crates; hold still until it's done) and bring it back to the bench at camp. Feed the fire with wood or fuel — the creature won't walk into its light, and a bigger fire (5 levels) pushes the fog back further. At the bench, [1]–[8] make things and [U] builds the bench up. In the woods: [1] set a bear trap (it holds the creature in place — pick traps back up with ), [2] a noise lure, [3] a flare, [4] eat, [5] a lantern post. Hold your torch beam on its face to drive it off. Find the four lost campers and walk them back to the fire. [J]: your goals (they pay coins and stay done). The run is saved at every dawn (CONTINUE in the briefing). No weapons, no map; it hunts by sound — crouch (), open doors crouched, and when the insects stop, it's close.
      • Mecha Camo: [L] locks you in place to paint: drag on yourself to paint (FINE/S/M/L brushes, [ and ] to change), drag anywhere else or right-drag to turn round yourself from any angle, scroll to zoom, click a wall to pick up its colour, [L] again to move. [Esc] or [B] opens the whole paint shop (FILL A PIECE, patterns with the 2nd colour, mixing). picks up the colour of what you face; is the chameleon spray (each part of you, the colour behind it). A yellow ? over the Warden: something caught its eye. A red !: it's hunting. HOLD STILL when it's close — if it walks away, that's a CLOSE CALL (and coins). [Shift] toggles the over-the-shoulder camera (or [L]); run with Space; pauses. The CAMO meter grades how well you blend in where you stand (from 8 directions, against what's behind you, lit as it's lit, and which side of you faces each way): EXCELLENT, GOOD or POOR. Hold at a breaker panel to throw it; lobs a paint can to pull the Warden away. Stay put too long and it smells you. Each round the Warden has a temperament (STALKER, PROWLER or LISTENER), something happens part-way through (BLACKOUT, SEARCHLIGHT DRONE, THE SLEEPWALKER, FRESH COAT — named on screen), three gold paint tins are hidden (they unlock paints), and there's a bonus job. Caged online: calls for help, watches a teammate. Two maps: Sublevel 6 and THE COLOUR WORKS (pick on the briefing screen, or the host picks online) — in the Works, in a SPRAY BOOTH coats you in its colours.
      • Mecha Camo emotes: [Z] opens the emote wheel — wave, dance, laugh, point, celebrate, facepalm, a nervous look, a fake faint (1–8, a click, or aim with the mouse and let go of Z; Esc closes it). Your team sees them. Moving stops one; the ♪ ones can be heard, and a big one in its sight counts as moving.
      • Mecha Camo, living maps: new round events — COLOUR SHIFT (the lamps change colour: only light and dark show, so match how bright the wall is), POWER SURGE (a flare that lets it see further, then the dark), EMERGENCY DOORS (Sublevel 6: a lockdown seals some doors for a while — never trapping anyone) and PAINT SPILL (the Colour Works: wet feet take the colour and leave footprints it follows). Props on the floor clatter if you run into them; the big red button starts a loud machine somewhere else to draw it away.
      • Cosmetic Locker (title screen): hats, masks, back pieces, body effects, paint jobs, footsteps and victory moves for your stickman, in six rarities. Earn them by playing (each one says how), find the secret on each camo map, or use the Cosmetic Roll (350 coins — odds printed, never a duplicate). Looks only: they never change your camo score, hitbox or speed.
      • Warden vs Guards (online): in the lobby, with MECHA CAMO picked, the host can choose to play the Warden: they wait in the dark while you hide, then hunt in first person — click to grab, [F] to sniff (everyone within 9 m shows for a moment, every 20 s). They see no meter and no cosmetics: only your paint.
      • Halloween (15 Oct – 2 Nov): five jack-o'-lanterns are hidden each run (Night Shift, Polaroids, Endless Night, Mecha Camo) — candy is +15 coins each, and all five in one run is the Pumpkin Head. The Warden dresses up too.
      • Panic Mode (every mode): when it's close — and can see you, or is after you — the edges of the screen pulse red with your heartbeat. Get away from something that was right on top of you and it's a CLOSE CALL (coins at the end, up to 10 a run). Settings → Panic effects / Heartbeat sound / Camera shake / Reduce flashing turn it down or off.
      • The Watch: opens the cameras (1–0, the arrow keys or the map to switch; again to look up). The red switch on the desk opens and shuts the door. The Warden shows up on CAM 05 or CAM 06 before your door — shut it in time and it slams it and goes. The Mannequin only moves while nobody watches it (a camera, or your own eyes through the doorway): check CAM 10 before you open the door. The brood comes down the vent: hold your light on the grate. Cameras and a shut door burn power; at 0% everything goes dark and the door won't hold.
      • The Night Shift: survive until 6:00 AM (the clock is at the top of the screen), then get onto the surface lift when the day shift opens it. Every hour it gets faster and sharper-eared; at 4:00 a power surge blacks everything out; in the last hour it can crawl into the vents. Or open the lift early: three keycards, main power and the breach report.
      • It hunts by sound and sight — and it has sharp ears. Walking near it is enough; when it hears you it runs to the sound. Crouch close to it, and hide the moment it starts running.
      • Your flashlight makes you visible from far away — and shining it at the Warden enrages it.
      • Its eyes give it away: pale when wandering, amber when investigating, red when hunting.
      • Break line of sight, close doors behind you and hide in lockers. It comes for your locker if it watched you get in, if it lost you right next to it, or if it stops outside and decides to try the door — then you have to hold the door shut. And you can only hold your nerve so long in there.
      • Crouch to crawl through the maintenance vents. Until 5:00 they are too small for it.
      • Cornered? Fight. Punches won't kill it, but they stagger it, and a stun buys you a few seconds. It shrugs off a second stun for a while — and comes back angrier.
      • Weapons. There's a crowbar on the security desk where you wake up. The other four glow orange where they lie and are marked orange on your map: a fire axe behind glass (Generator Hall), a shotgun (Containment — deafening, everything hears it), a flare gun (Camera Control) that sets it on fire and lights up the dark, and molotovs (Break Room) that leave a pool of fire it has to walk through. The bonus list under your objectives names the closest one you can reach, and H mentions it too. Face it with any weapon in your hand — even the crowbar — and time all but stops: FIGHT or RUN? Press E (or click) to fight and the Last Dance begins: it has a health bar now. Press Space or Shift to run, and the night goes on as normal — you'll get the choice again the next time you face it. Hits while it's staggered do extra damage; at half health it gets enraged. In the Night Shift, kill it and the shift is over. In the other modes nothing stays dead — it gets back up.
      • Hold the door. When it grabs your locker door, a strip of notes slides in: press Space every time a pull reaches the bar — on the beat. Mashing doesn't help. Miss too many and it's in. While it's at your door your nerve holds.
      • The heartbeat, flickering lights and the threat eye (top right) tell you when it is close.
      • Look up. In the long hallways it often climbs the wall and crawls along the ceiling, and it drops down on whoever is underneath. And it is cunning: a crash or a screech from one direction can be bait while it circles round to come at you from another.
      • Sometimes it just watches you from the dark. Hold its gaze and it backs off — walk toward it, or put your light on it, and it charges.
      • The Sleepwalker comes out of the Morgue at about 2:30. It is slow and it never hunts you — it just drifts from room to room humming a lullaby, and the lights dim around it. But near it you hallucinate: the room warps, you hear things that aren't there, the clock lies, and you see the Warden where it isn't (look straight at it and it vanishes). Never let it drift into you: it shrieks, your light dies — and the Warden hears.
      • On Hard the Warden breaks through locked iron security doors. Only the blast door to the lift holds.
      • Read every note. They contain the codes, routes and secrets you need to get out.
      • Bonus goals (under your objectives): six voice logs hidden around the level tell its story; rebooting the cameras in Camera Control puts it on your minimap (the reboot is loud); and you can learn who it used to be. Every shift ends with a score and a rank, and every achievement is saved under Goals, with your best times for every mode.
      • Co-op (up to 4): one player hosts and sends the invite link (or the 4-letter room code); friends open it and press Join. Keycards are shared, the Warden hunts whoever it notices, and a caught guard wakes up at Desk B — unless the whole team goes down.
